scope: Opt-in structural DOM diagnostics for the tested local browser automation failure path

implementation.transport: Native DOM.getDocument through the pinned Playwright 1.63.0 sync-to-async bridge.
implementation.time: 300 ms DOM sub-budget within the original caller-derived capture deadline capped at 2 seconds; creation, send, detach and cancellation use remaining absolute time.
implementation.cancellation: Explicit owned tasks and finite waits; first cancellation enters Playwright abort, a delivered second cancellation ends an unacknowledged abort wait. Unexpected nonterminal cleanup stops package publication.
implementation.retained_artifact: At most 160 visited nodes, depth 8 and 8192 bytes of actual LF-encoded formatted JSON. Only allowlisted tag/role enums and parent relationships remain.
implementation.privacy: Text, input values, IDs, names, URLs, arbitrary attributes, custom tag names, subframe and shadow-root content are omitted. Large role values are length-checked before lookup.
implementation.existing_guards: Screenshot uses remaining original budget; cancellation removes incomplete packages. Retention stays 30 days and 20 captures per application.

validation.real_browser: Three Chromium cases require captured form/input topology, complete visual/serialized redaction, 1000-node retained caps, and bounded omitted capture plus successful subsequent capture when owned DOM/abort acknowledgements are withheld.
validation.native_protocol: Installed Channel._inner_send, Connection._abort and ProtocolCallback are used for stalled creation/send/detach regressions; owned callback is canceled, shared transport future untouched, zero pending operation tasks.
validation.independent_review: Source and actual pinned-method review PASS; no remaining blocking source finding. This is internal review, not human approval.

resolved_intermediate_findings.finding: Initial asyncio.wait_for could wait indefinitely for Playwright abort acknowledgement.
resolved_intermediate_findings.resolution: Explicit finite two-phase task cancellation, verified against the actual installed protocol and real Chromium transport.

resolved_intermediate_findings.finding: Initial Windows JSON file was 8628 bytes despite an 8192-byte LF estimate.
resolved_intermediate_findings.resolution: Atomic JSON writer now forces LF; the actual disk-byte regression and Chromium size assertion pass.

resolved_intermediate_findings.finding: Broader local browser run exposed a historical changed-profile test that revoked all answers but expected automation to continue.
resolved_intermediate_findings.resolution: Baseline failure reproduced; separate frozen-contact and revoked-answer cases pass with production safety unchanged.

limitations: MJ-REQ-179 remains PARTIAL; complete browser-automation and real-adapter coverage is not established.
Raw CDP response bytes are decoded before retained node/byte limits; this is not a raw transport-size cap.
Synchronous filesystem operations are checkpointed but not hard-preempted.
The existing failure owner closes its browser context; no global connection/process teardown was added.
No external employer submission, paid AI call or live database restore was performed.
